annotations.description: MiMo Johnny ended turn 1 with 8 cards in hand and no permanents on the battlefield, meaning they missed their land drop (Seat of the Synod) and failed to play any of their three 0-cost artifacts (Lotus Petal, 2x Mishra's Bauble). This forces a discard and puts them an entire turn behind. Playing Seat of the Synod + Lotus Petal + both Baubles would have set up a turn 2 Emry (with 3 artifacts reducing her cost to just U) or Patchwork Automaton with counters.

annotations.betterLine: Play Seat of the Synod, cast Lotus Petal, cast both Mishra's Baubles (sacrificing them for value), then have a strong turn 2 with Emry costing just U or deploying Patchwork Automaton with artifact spell triggers

annotations.description: Attacking with Emry for 1 damage instead of using her tap ability to recast an artifact from the graveyard. The graveyard contains Lavaspur Boots and Mishra's Bauble, both of which could provide more value than 1 damage. With Metalcraft active (enabling Mox Opal), there was mana available to cast recovered artifacts.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Emry, Lurker of the Loch for 1 damage
annotations.betterLine: Keep Emry back, use her tap ability to target Lavaspur Boots or Mishra's Bauble in the graveyard, then cast it for additional board presence/card advantage

annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Emry, Lurker of the Loch for 1 damage
annotations.betterLine: Keep Emry back, tap her to target Mishra's Bauble in graveyard, then cast it for free to get a card draw next upkeep. 1 damage is negligible compared to recurring artifacts from the graveyard.

annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mox Opal, then Warp-cast Pinnacle Emissary (which gets exiled at end of turn with no value generated).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Patchwork Automaton (using Seat of the Synod + Lotus Petal for {2}), then cast Mox Opal to give Patchwork a +1/+1 counter, leaving a permanent 2/2 with ward 2 that continues to grow.

The stated reasoning about returning Expedition Map from graveyard is also completely wrong - Kozilek's Command cannot do that. The mana would be better saved or the turn used differently to set up casting a 4-drop next turn.

annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mishra's Bauble before deploying Patchwork Automaton

annotations.description: Mishra's Bauble's activated ability lets you look at the top card of a target player's library. Targeting yourself is almost always better than targeting the opponent, because knowing what you'll draw next helps you plan your turns (especially with Emry decisions and whether to cast things from graveyard). Looking at the opponent's top card provides marginal information - you see one card they might draw but can't do anything about it. Looking at your own top card helps you sequence your plays optimally.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted GLM47 Analyst with Mishra's Bauble, looking at the opponent's top card.
annotations.betterLine: Target yourself with Mishra's Bauble to see your own top card, which helps plan future turns - especially relevant with Emry's graveyard casting ability and deciding whether to use mana on graveyard artifacts or wait for draws.

annotations.description: GLM47 Analyst had exactly enough mana to cast Tezzeret, Cruel Captain (costs {3}) by using the Candelabra + Voltaic Key untap chain to generate 3 colorless mana, but instead passed the turn doing nothing with a full hand of powerful spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Candelabra of Tawnos or Voltaic Key, passing the turn with no plays.
annotations.betterLine: Tap both lands for {C}{C}, activate Candelabra (X=1) to untap a land, tap it again, use Voltaic Key to untap Candelabra, activate Candelabra (X=1) to untap a land again, tap it for a total of 3 mana, then cast Tezzeret, Cruel Captain. Tezzeret could immediately use -3 to fetch a 0-1 cost artifact, gaining metalcraft and board presence.

annotations.description: MiMo Johnny already has Emry, Lurker of the Loch on the battlefield. Casting a second copy from hand will legend-rule one of them away, meaning they sacrifice the original Emry (which is already untapped and ready to use) just to get a fresh ETB mill trigger and a new summoning-sick Emry. While the mill is nice, they're wasting a card from hand for minimal benefit. Meanwhile, they have Patchwork Automaton (a 2-mana play that grows with artifact casts and has ward 2) or could set up Pinnacle Emissary via Warp for just U/R, both of which would develop the board without sacrificing an existing creature. Emry could also be used to activate her tap ability targeting Lavaspur Boots or Mishra's Bauble in the graveyard before being replaced, but casting the legend immediately wastes the existing copy's tap ability for this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a second Emry, Lurker of the Loch from hand while one was already on the battlefield, legend-ruling the original away.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Patchwork Automaton (which grows with each artifact cast and has ward 2) to develop the board, or use existing Emry's tap ability to recur Lavaspur Boots or Mishra's Bauble from graveyard first, then consider if the second Emry is even needed.

annotations.description: MiMo Johnny could have cast Kappa Cannoneer using Improvise by tapping Seat of the Synod for {U} and tapping 5 artifacts (Mox Opal, Urza's Bauble, 2 Drone Tokens, existing Patchwork Automaton) for the generic {5}. Kappa Cannoneer would enter as a 5/5 (gets +1/+1 counter from itself entering), be unblockable that turn, and have ward 4 making it very hard to remove. Instead they cast a 1/1 Patchwork Automaton and attacked for only 3.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Patchwork Automaton (a 1/1) and attacked with existing Patchwork Automaton + Drone Token for 3 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kappa Cannoneer using Improvise (tap 5 artifacts + Seat of the Synod for U), attack with it as an unblockable 5/5 for 5 damage, applying significant pressure with a ward 4 threat.

annotations.description: MiMo Johnny declined to activate Emry, Lurker of the Loch, missing the line of targeting Lotus Petal in graveyard, casting it for free, then using Seat of the Synod ({U}) + Mox Opal ({C}) + Lotus Petal ({C}) + tapping 3 remaining artifacts for Improvise to cast Kappa Cannoneer (a 4/4 with ward 4 that would enter with a +1/+1 counter and be unblockable this turn). This would have dealt 5 damage and established a massive threat. Additionally, Urza's Bauble could have been sacrificed for free card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities during combat, passing the turn without developing the board.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emry targeting Lotus Petal in graveyard, cast Lotus Petal (free), then cast Kappa Cannoneer using Seat of the Synod + Mox Opal + Lotus Petal + Improvise from remaining artifacts, attacking for 5 unblockable damage this turn.

annotations.description: Attacking with the two Drone Tokens (0/1 creatures dealing 0 damage) taps them, preventing their use as Improvise sources for Kappa Cannoneer. With Seat of the Synod (U) + Mox Opal (1) + Urza's Bauble (Improvise) + 2 Drone Tokens (Improvise), MiMo Johnny could have exactly cast Kappa Cannoneer ({5}{U}) in the second main phase. Attacking with 0-power tokens for no damage gain cost the ability to deploy a powerful 4/4 ward 4 threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures including both 0/1 Drone Tokens, tapping them for 0 total damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Emry and Patchwork Automaton (3 damage), keep Drone Tokens untapped to use as Improvise sources, then cast Kappa Cannoneer in second main phase using Seat of the Synod + Mox Opal + Improvise (Urza's Bauble + 2 Drone Tokens).

annotations.description: Mystic Forge is a powerful card advantage engine that would let the opponent (who has Urza lands generating lots of mana) chain artifacts and colorless spells from the top of their library, potentially finding The One Ring or other game-changing cards. Despite being ahead on board with the opponent at 9 life, letting this resolve risks the opponent stabilizing and overwhelming MiMo Johnny with card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Mystic Forge, letting it resolve
annotations.betterLine: Cast Force of Will (exiling the second Force of Will or a Kappa Cannoneer) to counter Mystic Forge, preventing the opponent's card advantage engine from coming online while maintaining board pressure to close out the game

annotations.description: At 1 life, activating The One Ring in response to its upkeep trigger adds a burden counter. When the upkeep trigger resolves, it counts burden counters at resolution time, meaning the added counter causes lethal damage. If there were 0 counters before, the trigger would have dealt 0 and they'd survive; now it deals 1 and they die.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated The One Ring to draw cards in response to its upkeep life-loss trigger
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate The One Ring. Let the upkeep trigger resolve (dealing damage based on existing burden counters). If 0 counters, survive and proceed to draw step. If 1+ counters, dead either way but at least don't make it worse.
